summary: Extends the RIB YANG model from RFC 8349 so each route can have multiple next hops and additional attributes. It helps management systems represent and configure routing information.

eli5.summary: A route list used to show one way to go. This lets it show several ways, with notes on each.

subtitle: Enhanced route model supporting multiple next hops and additional attributes.

tldr.problem: RFC 8349 defines basic routing information base (RIB) data for network management, but lacks support for multiple next hops per route and advanced route attributes needed by modern routing systems.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9403 augments the RIB model with support for multiple next hops per route, per-next-hop preferences and tags, route metrics, repair paths for fast reroute, and RIB statistics.
tldr.outcome: Network operators can now represent complex routing configurations and monitor detailed RIB information through YANG data models managed via standard protocols.

today: RFC 9403 is an Internet Standard and remains the current model for expressing advanced RIB attributes in YANG-based routing management.

sections.title: The Routing Information Base
sections.content:
A Routing Information Base (RIB) is the core data structure that routers use to make forwarding decisions. It contains a list of network destinations with the next hops to reach them. Each route also has administrative attributes like the protocol that installed it and its administrative distance (preference). RFC 8349 defined a YANG data model for the basic RIB; RFC 9403 extends it to handle more complex real-world routing scenarios.

The YANG data model allows network management systems to query and configure routing information via standard protocols like NETCONF and RESTCONF, making routing visible and manageable rather than hidden inside device proprietary systems.
sections.eli5: A routing table is like a map that tells a router where to send packets. This extension lets the map show multiple ways to go, and notes about which are better and what to do if one breaks.

sections.title: Augmentation Strategy
sections.content:
Rather than replace RFC 8349, RFC 9403 augments it by adding new containers and leaf nodes to existing structures. This allows existing code that uses the base model to coexist with applications that need the enhanced features. The model augments both static route configuration (under control-plane-protocols) and the RIB data itself (under ribs).

The augmentations follow NMDA (Network Management Datastore Architecture) conventions, distinguishing between configuration data (read-write) that administrators set, and operational state data (read-only) that reflects the current RIB state.
sections.eli5: Instead of rebuilding the whole routing model, this just adds extra fields to the existing one. So old systems keep working, but new systems can use the extra information.

sections.title: Tags, Preferences, and Route Selection
sections.content:
The model augments static route configuration to add two new per-next-hop attributes:

  • Preference: A 32-bit value (default 1) that ranks next hops when multiple paths exist to the same destination. Lower preference values are preferred; equal preferences enable Equal-Cost Multipath (ECMP) load balancing.
  • Tag: A 32-bit opaque value (default 0) that can carry policy information for use in route filtering or redistribution between protocols.

Routes in the RIB itself also carry a metric (cost) per route for protocols that do not have their own metric augmentations. Route-level tags support policy decisions across many next hops. An additional application-tag field lets applications assign their own semantic meaning to routes.
sections.eli5: Each route can have a preference number saying how much better one way is than another. Tags are like labels that network managers can use to group routes or apply rules to them.

sections.title: Fast Reroute and Repair Paths
sections.content:
IP Fast Reroute (IPFRR) is a technique where a router precomputes an alternate next hop to use if the primary next hop fails, allowing fast local recovery without waiting for routing protocols to converge. RFC 9403 augments each RIB next hop with a repair-path container that holds the backup route information:

  • Outgoing interface: The interface to use for the repair path
  • Next-hop address: The IP address of the alternate next hop
  • Metric: The cost of the repair path, useful for troubleshooting

Repair paths are read-only in the RIB, set by the routing protocols that precompute them. Both simple next hops and next-hop lists can have repair paths.
sections.eli5: When a router has a backup route ready to use instantly if the main route breaks, it stores that backup information here. It helps the router recover from failures faster.

sections.title: RIB Statistics and Monitoring
sections.content:
The model augments each RIB with a statistics container providing visibility into RIB contents and resource use. Top-level statistics include:

  • Total routes: Count of all routes in the RIB
  • Total active routes: Count of routes selected as preferred over alternatives to the same destination
  • Total route memory: Bytes of memory consumed by RIB data

Per-protocol statistics break down the same numbers by which routing protocol installed each route, showing which protocols contribute how many routes and which ones are active. This helps operators understand the composition and resource consumption of their routing tables.
sections.eli5: The router can tell you how many routes it has, how many it is actually using, and how much memory they take up. You can also see which routing protocols contributed which routes.

sections.title: Integration with Existing Models
sections.content:
RFC 9403 augments the core routing modules (ietf-routing, ietf-ipv4-unicast-routing, ietf-ipv6-unicast-routing) defined in RFC 8349. It also coordinates with protocol-specific models: the metric augmentation includes a when statement that excludes OSPF and IS-IS routes, since RFC 9129 and RFC 9130 already define their own metric augmentations. This avoids duplication and confusion.

The combined tree shows how all these pieces fit together, giving a complete view of routing configuration and state in a network management system.
sections.eli5: This model works alongside other routing models for specific protocols. It doesn't duplicate information that OSPF and ISIS already provide.

sections.title: Use Today
sections.content: RFC 9403 is an Internet Standard published in November 2023. It is used by vendors implementing comprehensive YANG-based routing management for systems that need to represent complex route attributes and fast reroute configurations. Network operators can use this model to query and manage RIB data in a standardized way across multi-vendor networks.
sections.eli5: This is the official standard way to describe advanced routing information and is available for use today.

items.title: Preference
items.text: Lower value preferred; equal values enable ECMP.
